clue.text: Island state shown in unusually accurate burlesque

indicators.note: the island state's letters are displayed inside the jumbled word
the word accurate is set out in an unusual order

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state named as an island

explanation.surface: A small island nation is portrayed in a parody that is surprisingly faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges ACCURATE to CACATURE; 'shown in' puts RI inside it after CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a mocking exaggeration of something, just as a cartoon lampoon is.

clue.text: Found direction in class

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
E for east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone discovered which way to go while in a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid hereditary social rank, as in Hindu society, is a class.

clue.text: A sheet from Paddy's Journal?

parts.note: a paddy is a flooded field in which a grain is grown, so its crop is the paddy's own
a journal is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: A page torn from an Irishman's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irishman, but here is the flooded field where the grain is grown; 'from' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin edible sheets made from a grain grown in paddy fields are used in cooking and for painting.

clue.text: At which gamblers made five bob once with a couple of flukes

parts.note: a crown was an old British coin worth five shillings, five bob in slang
with means and, joining things together
an anchor has two flukes, the pointed blades on its arms

explanation.surface: Gamblers once won five shillings with a pair of lucky shots.
explanation.walkthrough: A crown was a pre-decimal British coin worth five shillings ('bob'); the named game is an old dice game played by sailors, its dice marked with symbols including those two.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old dice game, popular with sailors, on which players bet money.

clue.text: Delayed, thanks to rider's mishap

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: a mishap throws the word rider into disorder

parts.note: the word rider, with the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A hold-up was caused because a horseman had an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mishap' rearranges RIDER to RRIED, following TA.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lingered or stayed on is to have delayed.

clue.text: Right in the matter of costume

parts.note: re means concerning, in the matter of
a costume is a dress

explanation.surface: A remark about the proper choice of fancy dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to remedy or correct it.

clue.text: Olympian land measures

definitions.meaning: the Greek god of war, one of the gods on Mount Olympus
metric units of area, each a hundred square metres

explanation.surface: A Greek god measures out the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The war god of Greek myth lived on Olympus; separately, the metric unit of area of one hundred square metres has this plural.

clue.text: Ransack the Spanish wood up here

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
fir is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Plunder the Spanish timber up in these parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ELFIR backwards to give the answer; 'here' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To search thoroughly and steal from a place is to ransack it.

clue.text: Jack Ketch's item of underwear

definitions.meaning: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English hangman, so his trade made him one who hangs people up
a garter worn to hold up stockings or socks

explanation.surface: A hangman's pair of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangman literally hangs people, and a garter holding up stockings is a British term for underwear.

clue.text: Exclude pop? I'm so crazy with this thing about mum

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of the preceding words are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: A son rejecting his father, mad and obsessed with his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges EXCLUDE POP IM SO; the 'pop' versus 'mum' surface fits Freud's idea perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's term for a child's desire for the opposite-sex parent, named after the Greek king who married his mother.

clue.text: Dupe is heard calling for help

indicators.note: is heard means the word for dupe is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person, a dupe

explanation.surface: A gullible victim is overheard crying out for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance or relief given in time of need is help.

clue.text: Ed's fury uncontrolled, as was Zola's on his behalf

definitions.text: Ed's fury uncontrolled, as was Zola's on his behalf

indicators.note: uncontrolled means the letters of the words before run wild

explanation.surface: Ed loses his temper, as Zola did when defending someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrolled' rearranges EDSFURY. Zola's famous open letter J'accuse furiously defended the Jewish army officer wrongly convicted of treason in 1894.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola wrote J'accuse in angry defence of the French army captain wrongly jailed for espionage.

clue.text: Dear girl accommodates team that includes writers

indicators.note: accommodates means the girl's name holds the rest within it

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: that includes means the team's letters wrap around the writers

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a team such as in football or cricket
pens are writing implements

explanation.surface: A beloved woman puts up a squad that contains some authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of costly, high-priced.

clue.text: According to Holmes the woman's first name

definitions.text: According to Holmes the woman's first name

parts.words: According to Holmes the woman's first name
parts.note: Sherlock Holmes always called Adler, the opera singer who outwitted him, simply 'the woman', and this is her given name

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes reveals what a lady is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Adler, the adventuress in A Scandal in Bohemia whom Holmes called 'the woman', bears this given name.

clue.text: Could the coot, with this bird, conceal its baldness?

definitions.text: Could the coot, with this bird, conceal its baldness?

parts.words: Could the coot, with this bird, conceal its baldness?
parts.note: bald as a coot is a saying; the bird could hide its bald head by putting a hat over it, and the castrated cockerel's name splits into those two words

explanation.surface: Might a bald waterbird cover its head with the help of another bird?
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a bird.

clue.text: Message for taxi to take member to music school

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
RAM is the Royal Academy of Music in London

explanation.surface: A request for a taxi to bring a pupil to the conservatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram sent by undersea cable was a message.

clue.text: Doctor outside is taking up boy, being violently disturbed

indicators.note: outside means the doctor's letters sit around the next word

parts.note: taken as written
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A physician outside picks up a lad who has been badly shaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown into confusion and upset by force is the sense of the participle.

clue.text: Restaurant serves up jammy confection to one in the gunners

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pastry's letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a jam tart is a pastry with jam filling
taken as written

indicators.note: in means one is placed within the gunners' letters

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An eatery offers a jam pastry to a soldier in the artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serves up' turns TART to TRAT; I goes 'in' RA.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian eating house is a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Give us a haircut, say, that's crude

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a request to barber us, to cut our hair

explanation.surface: Asking for a trim in a rough manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barber us' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncivilised and coarse is crude.

clue.text: Work on newspapers can so get one down

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Working on the papers can be depressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To burden or weigh heavily on someone is to get them down.

clue.text: Vegetable with gammon for Anthony Rowley

definitions.text: Vegetable with gammon for Anthony Rowley

parts.words: Vegetable with gammon for Anthony Rowley
parts.note: in the nursery song A Frog He Would A-Wooing Go, the refrain pairs gammon with a leafy green, followed by heigh-ho says Anthony Rowley

explanation.surface: A side dish to go with ham for a man named Anthony Rowley.
explanation.walkthrough: Gammon is a cured ham; the song's chorus is 'With a rowley powley gammon and ... heigh-ho! says Anthony Rowley'.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy green plant eaten cooked or raw is a vegetable.

clue.text: Church music taken by the president

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: Church music is played by the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: The person presiding over a meeting is its president.

clue.text: Moral code — of Christians for instance, and here in Rome

definitions.text: Moral code — of Christians for instance

parts.note: et is Latin for and, the language of Rome
hic is Latin for here

explanation.surface: A moral standard, perhaps Christian, which also applies here in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Rome' tells you both words are Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of moral principles, such as the Protestant work one, is a moral code.

clue.text: Dog — or horse, say?

definitions.meaning: a sled dog of the Arctic
horse sounds like hoarse, which means having a rough voice

explanation.surface: Is it a dog or a horse?
explanation.definitionFit: An Arctic sled dog has this name; it also means hoarse, which sounds like horse.

clue.text: Did Miss Cardew's governess appear in such rainbow colours?

definitions.text: Did Miss Cardew's governess appear in such rainbow colours?

parts.words: Did Miss Cardew's governess appear in such rainbow colours?
parts.note: in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, Cecily Cardew's governess is Miss Prism, so an adjective formed from her name means rainbow-hued

explanation.surface: Did a governess from a Wilde play wear brightly coloured clothes?
explanation.definitionFit: Light passing through a glass prism splits into the colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: In which Hiawatha finally went West

definitions.text: In which Hiawatha finally went West

parts.words: In which Hiawatha finally went West
parts.note: at the end of Longfellow's poem, Hiawatha departs westward in his birch-bark boat; to go west is also to die

explanation.surface: How Longfellow's hero met his end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiawatha paddles off into the sunset in a light boat at the close of the poem.

clue.text: 20's tail is only item on the menu

indicators.note: tail means the last letter of the answer to clue 20 across

parts.note: 20 refers to the answer to clue 20 across, the presiding officer's seat
taken as written
sole means only, single

explanation.surface: The end of an earlier answer is the one dish available.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried cake of minced meat or fish is a dish on a menu.

clue.text: Aircraft control obtainable from retailer only

indicators.note: obtainable from means the letters can be got out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plane's part sold by just one shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged flap on an aircraft wing that controls roll.

clue.text: Girl of the month a one-time Mexican Indian?

parts.note: May is a month of the year

explanation.surface: A girl born in spring is said to be from an ancient people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl of the' adds that Maya is also a girl's name, making a near double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Central American people of Yucatán were a Mexican Indian civilisation.

clue.text: He pays taxi — odd way to get rid of Desdemona!

indicators.note: odd way means the letters are set in a strange arrangement

explanation.surface: A man settles a cab fare, an odd method of disposing of Othello's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd way' rearranges HE PAYS TAXI; Othello smothers Desdemona in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello kills his wife by smothering her, cutting off her air.
